rationale: C10 is an unmistakable material drafting template. The child reproduces its personnel policies, written-certification requirements, Federal Register filing procedure, treatment of prior appointments, quarterly Civil Service Commission review, and detailed conflict-of-interest exemptions, while adapting the machinery from Defense Production Act personnel to Federal Civil Defense Act personnel. C11 is also relevant because the child incorporates its amendments limiting written certification to non-advisory or non-consultative positions and narrowing the salary restriction, but C10 supplies the main body and sequence. C09 is a distant third because it contains related delegation and Classification Act machinery underlying C10, without the child's distinctive operative sequence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: So far as possible, Federal operations under the Act shall be carried on by full-time, salaried employees of the Government, and appointments under this authority shall be limited to advisory or consultative positions only.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: So far as possible, operations under the Act shall be carried on by full-time, salaried employees of the Government, and appointments under this authority shall be to advisory or consultative positions only.
shared_material.explanation: Near-verbatim personnel policy, adapted only by adding “Federal” and slightly changing the final phrasing.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Appointments to positions other than advisory or consultative shall be made only when the requirements of the position are such that the incumbent must personally possess outstanding experience and ability not obtainable on a full-time, salaried basis.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Appointments to positions other than advisory or consultative may be made under this order only when the requirements of the position are such that the incumbent must personally possess outstanding experience and ability not obtainable on a full-time, salaried basis.
shared_material.explanation: The child closely copies C10's distinctive substantive limitation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: shall be supported by written certification by the Administrator: (a) That the appointment is necessary and appropriate in order to carry out the provisions of the Act; (b) That the duties ... require outstanding experience and ability; (c) That the appointee has the outstanding experience and ability required ...; and (d) That the Administrator has been unable to obtain a person ... on a full-time, salaried basis.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: shall be supported by written certification by the head of the employing department or agency: (a) That the appointment is necessary and appropriate in order to carry out the provisions of the Act; (b) That the duties ... require outstanding experience and ability; (c) That the appointee has the outstanding experience and ability required ...; and (d) That the department or agency head has been unable to obtain a person ... on a full-time, salaried basis.
shared_material.explanation: The same four-part certification test appears in the same order, with the responsible official changed to the Civil Defense Administrator.

shared_material.child_excerpt: shall file with the Division of the Federal Register (for public inspection but not for publication) a statement including the name of the appointee, the section of the Act under which he was appointed, the title of his position, and the name of his private employer.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: shall file with the Division of the Federal Register (for public inspection but not for publication) a statement including the name of the appointee, the section of this order under which he was appointed, the employing department or agency, the title of his position, and the name of his private employer.
shared_material.explanation: The child reuses C10's distinctive filing mechanism and nearly all enumerated data fields.

shared_material.child_excerpt: At least once every three months, the Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission shall survey appointments made under this part and shall report his findings to the President and make such recommendations as he may deem proper.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: At least once every three months, the Chairman of the United States Civil Service Commission shall survey appointments made under this order and shall report his findings to the President and make such recommendations as he may deem proper.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Any person employed under the authority conferred upon the Administrator ... is hereby exempted ... from the operation of sections 281, 283, 284, 434, and 1914 of Title 18, United States Code, and section 190 of the Revised Statutes ... except as specified in the following subsections
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Any person employed under Part I of this order is hereby exempted ... from the operation of sections 281, 283, 284, 434, and 1914 of Title 18, United States Code, and section 190 of the Revised Statutes ... except as specified in the following subsections
shared_material.explanation: The child carries over the same statutory exemptions and then adapts C10's detailed exceptions concerning private employers, claims against the Government, outside salary, and particular classes of appointees.
